senses.gloss: A person whose job is to look after animals, a place, or a collection.
examples: The zoo *keeper* hand-raised the tiger cub.
*Keepers* at the lighthouse logged every ship that passed.
She is the *keeper* of all the family photographs.

senses.gloss: The player who guards the goal in soccer or hockey.
examples: Their *keeper* stopped three shots in the second half.
The ball went right past the *keeper*.
Both *keepers* played the whole game.

senses.gloss: An informal word for someone or something good enough to hold on to.
senses.ru: то, что стоит сохранить; отличный вариант
examples: This soup recipe is a *keeper*.
Her new boyfriend seems like a *keeper*.
Out of fifty photos, only three were *keepers*.

senses.gloss: The central or most important part of an idea or a statement.
examples: There is a *kernel* of truth in what he said.
The whole company grew out of one *kernel* of an idea.
Strip away the jokes and you find a hard *kernel* of anger.

senses.gloss: The core part of a computer's operating system.
examples: The update fixes a security hole in the *kernel*.
Linux *kernels* are numbered by version.
A crash in the *kernel* takes down the whole machine.

senses.gloss: The thing that explains or solves something.
examples: Practice is the *key* to playing well.
Sleep turned out to be the *key* to his recovery.
That one letter was the *key* to the whole mystery.

senses.gloss: One of the buttons you press on a keyboard, a piano, or a phone.
examples: The S *key* on my laptop sticks.
He ran his fingers over the piano *keys*.
Press any *key* to continue.

senses.gloss: A list on a map or a chart explaining what its symbols mean.
examples: The *key* shows that a green triangle is a campground.
Read the *key* before you try to read the graph.
Both maps use the same *key*.

senses.gloss: The set of musical notes that a piece of music is built on.
examples: The song is in the *key* of G.
She sang it in a lower *key* to suit her voice.
The two pieces are in different *keys*.

senses.gloss: A feeling of pleasure or excitement.
examples: She gets a real *kick* out of watching the kids play.
He rides motorcycles for the *kick*.
I got a *kick* out of that movie.

senses.gloss: A short period of being very enthusiastic about one thing.
examples: He's on a health *kick* this month.
She's been on a baking *kick* since January.
My daughter is on a dinosaur *kick* right now.

senses.gloss: A young goat.
examples: The goat had two *kids* in the spring.
A newborn *kid* can stand up within an hour.
We bottle-fed the *kid* until it could graze.

senses.gloss: The act of killing, especially the closing moment of a hunt or a contest.
examples: The lions circled and then moved in for the *kill*.
Two goals ahead, the team went in for the *kill*.
The camera crew waited three days to film a *kill*.

senses.gloss: An informal word for something extremely hard, exhausting, or impressive.
senses.ru: нечто убойное (очень трудное или очень крутое)
examples: That last hill was a *killer*.
The final exam was a real *killer*.
Their new album is a *killer*.

senses.gloss: A large amount of money made quickly.
examples: They made a *killing* on that house.
He made a *killing* in the stock market last year.
A few early sellers made a *killing*.

senses.gloss: One of the largest groups that scientists divide living things into.
examples: Mushrooms belong to the fungus *kingdom*.
The animal *kingdom* runs from sponges to whales.
Biology once recognized only two *kingdoms*.

senses.gloss: A bird of prey with long narrow wings and a forked tail.
examples: A *kite* circled slowly over the field.
*Kites* often nest in tall trees near rivers.
We watched a *kite* snatch a fish off the water.

senses.gloss: A pool of money that several people put into for a shared purpose.
examples: Everyone put five dollars in the *kitty* for pizza.
The office *kitty* pays for coffee and snacks.
Whatever is left in the *kitty* gets split at the end.

senses.gloss: The chess piece shaped like a horse's head, which moves in an L shape.
examples: She moved her *knight* to threaten the queen.
A *knight* is the only piece that can jump over others.
He lost both *knights* in the first ten moves.

senses.gloss: A Labrador retriever, one of the most common family dogs in America.
examples: They adopted a chocolate *Lab* from the shelter.
*Labs* are friendly and easy to train.
Our yellow *Lab* swims in the lake all summer.

senses.gloss: A company that records and sells music.
examples: The band signed with a major *label*.
She started her own *label* after leaving the group.
Several independent *labels* are based in Nashville.

senses.gloss: A word used to describe a person or a group, often unfairly.
examples: He hates the *label* 'genius'.
Once a kid gets a *label* like that, it sticks.
She refuses all political *labels*.

senses.gloss: The process of giving birth, from the first contractions onward.
examples: She went into *labor* just after midnight.
*Labor* lasted almost fourteen hours.
He drove her to the hospital as soon as *labor* started.

senses.gloss: A series of ranks or levels that a person can move up.
examples: He worked his way up the corporate *ladder*.
Teacher pay follows a strict *ladder*.
Changing firms put her back at the bottom of the *ladder*.

senses.gloss: A private place where a person hides away or works undisturbed.
examples: The villain's *lair* was hidden inside a volcano.
His basement workshop is his *lair*.
Reporters finally tracked the billionaire to his mountain *lair*.

senses.gloss: Ground that someone owns, farms, or builds on.
examples: They bought forty acres of *land* outside town.
His family has farmed this *land* for a century.
The company owns *land* on both sides of the river.

senses.gloss: A country or region.
examples: America is still called a *land* of opportunity.
The story is set in a distant *land*.
Her grandparents came from a *land* she has never seen.

senses.gloss: The act of bringing an aircraft or a spacecraft down to the ground.
examples: The pilot made a smooth *landing* in heavy wind.
Bad weather forced an emergency *landing* in Denver.
The moon *landing* was watched by millions.

senses.gloss: A place on a shore where boats load and unload.
examples: We put the canoe in at the public boat *landing*.
The ferry *landing* is at the end of this road.
Kids were fishing off the old *landing*.

senses.gloss: One complete trip around a track or the length of a pool.
examples: He runs twenty *laps* every morning.
She swims *laps* before work.
The leader spun out on the final *lap*.

senses.gloss: A person or organization that obeys someone powerful without question.
examples: Critics called the agency a *lapdog* of the industry.
He refused to be anyone's *lapdog*.
The paper was accused of being a *lapdog* for the mayor.

senses.gloss: The ending of a right, policy, or membership because it was not kept up.
examples: A *lapse* in coverage can cost you a lot later.
There was a two-month *lapse* in his health insurance.
The *lapse* of the patent let other companies copy the drug.

senses.gloss: Something done just for fun or on a sudden whim.
examples: We drove to the coast on a *lark*.
He entered the contest as a *lark* and won.
What started as a *lark* turned into a real business.

senses.gloss: A blow with a whip.
examples: The sentence was forty *lashes*.
Every *lash* left a red mark across his back.
The driver gave the mule a *lash* to keep it moving.

senses.gloss: The sending of a rocket, missile, or satellite into the air.
examples: The *launch* was delayed by bad weather.
Thousands watched the rocket *launch* from the beach.
Two more *launches* are scheduled for next month.

senses.gloss: Honor or praise earned by an achievement, usually used in the plural.
examples: He has been resting on his *laurels* since the first book.
The team brought home new *laurels* from the state meet.
She earned those *laurels* the hard way.

senses.gloss: The thin gray stick inside a pencil that leaves the marks.
examples: The *lead* snapped as soon as I pressed down.
Mechanical pencils take thin refill *leads*.
Sharpen it until the *lead* comes to a point.

senses.gloss: The passing of secret information to the press or the public.
examples: The *leak* embarrassed the whole department.
Reporters ran the story on the strength of a *leak*.
A series of *leaks* revealed the plan weeks in advance.

senses.gloss: A long scolding about how someone ought to behave.
examples: I got a *lecture* from my dad about the car.
Spare me the *lecture*.
The coach gave the team a *lecture* about showing up late.

senses.gloss: A person who lives off other people's money or effort.
examples: Her cousin is a total *leech*.
He got tired of supporting a *leech*.
He called them *leeches* living off the family fortune.

senses.gloss: One of the upright supports that hold up a table, chair, or bed.
examples: One *leg* of the table is shorter than the others.
He screwed the *legs* onto the desk.
The chair wobbles because a *leg* is loose.

senses.gloss: One stage of a journey, race, or competition.
examples: The last *leg* of the trip took six hours.
She flew the first *leg* by herself.
They won both *legs* of the series.

senses.gloss: A very famous and admired person in some field.
examples: He is a *legend* in country music.
The old coach is a local *legend*.
Two boxing *legends* met in the ring that night.

senses.gloss: The part of a map or chart that explains what its symbols mean.
examples: The *legend* says a dotted line is a hiking trail.
Check the *legend* to see what the colors stand for.
Both charts share one *legend*.

senses.gloss: A car or product that turns out to be badly made and full of faults.
examples: The used car turned out to be a *lemon*.
State *lemon* laws protect people who buy new cars.
That printer was a *lemon* from day one.

senses.gloss: A piece cut from something long.
examples: He cut a *length* of rope for the swing.
Two *lengths* of pipe were left over.
She tied a *length* of ribbon around the box.

senses.gloss: The amount of time that something lasts.
examples: The *length* of the movie surprised me.
Our meetings vary in *length*.
There is a limit on the *length* of each visit.

senses.gloss: The clear part inside the eye that focuses light onto the retina.
examples: Surgeons replaced the clouded *lens* in her right eye.
The *lens* stiffens as a person gets older.
A cataract forms when the *lens* turns cloudy.

senses.gloss: A particular way of looking at or understanding something.
examples: He sees every issue through the *lens* of economics.
The book tells the war through the *lens* of ordinary soldiers.
Try looking at the problem through a different *lens*.

senses.gloss: Something useful that experience teaches you.
examples: Let that be a *lesson* to you.
The flood taught the town a hard *lesson*.
He learned his *lesson* about lending money to friends.

senses.gloss: One of the written signs that make up an alphabet.
examples: The word 'rhythm' has six *letters*.
She wrote her name in capital *letters*.
The last *letter* on the sign had fallen off.

senses.gloss: The amount, size, or degree of something measured against a scale.
examples: The river reached a record *level* on Tuesday.
Noise *levels* downtown keep rising.
Her stress *level* dropped after the move.

senses.gloss: A floor of a building or a parking garage.
examples: Shoes are on the second *level*.
I parked on *level* three.
The mall has four *levels*.

senses.gloss: A stage in a video game that a player must finish to reach the next.
examples: He can't get past *level* nine.
The final *level* takes about an hour.
Each *level* is harder than the one before.

senses.gloss: A secret romantic or sexual relationship.
examples: He denied any *liaison* with the actress.
Their *liaison* lasted a single summer.
The novel turns on a secret *liaison* between neighbors.
